drhp.business: Prakash Pipes Limited is a public limited company engaged primarily in manufacturing PVC pipes & fittings and flexible packaging. It sells its products in both the domestic and international markets, serving applications across irrigation, drainage, housing, plumbing and sanitation, as well as food, beverage, pharmaceutical and personal-care packaging.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Government focus on urbanization, infrastructure, irrigation, water conservation and waste water management expected to boost PVC pipe demand.
- Indian PVC pipe industry projected to grow at a CAGR of ~10-12% in FY27, driven by robust housing demand and infrastructure projects like Jal Jeevan Mission and Amrut 2.0.
- Union Budget 2026-27 allocated a large outlay to the Ministry of Jal Shakti targeting national water security.
- Domestic flexible packaging market projected to grow at CAGR ~11%, driven by e-commerce and quick commerce boom, food and pharma dominance, and rising per capita packaging …

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The flexible packaging division has taken up a capacity expansion plan in a phased manner, which is intended to enhance installed capacity substantially over the years, driven by strong demand potential, rising sales volumes and an expanding customer base in domestic and international markets. Separately, the Company is developing and installing a 3.9 MW solar power project at its manufacturing plant, and has acquired a 26% equity stake in BECIS Solar 3 Private Limited with a long-term Power Purchase Agreement for captive supply of power to its Kashipur, Uttarakhand production unit.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- High dependence on imported PVC resin exposes the business to crude oil price movements, currency depreciation, and higher working-capital requirements.
- Elevated costs and inflationary pressures could constrain demand from urban infrastructure, real estate, plumbing, and water-supply applications.
- Energy-price shocks, disruptions in West Asia, inflation and trade-policy uncertainty could affect input costs, investment, and end-user demand.
- Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations under plastic waste management regulations add compliance burden.
- The Company's borrowings (variable and fixed rate) expose it to fluctuations in market interest rates affecting future cash flows and fair value of financial instruments.
- Counterparty default risk on trade receivables; ageing data shows amounts overdue beyond 365 days with associated expected credit losses.
